one_liner: Research-grade multi-threaded CPU rasterizer for solid-color path fills; the author reports 2.6x faster than multi-threaded Blend2D (2023 version) on an M1 Max.
what_it_does: Blaze rasterizes an array of Geometry records into a premultiplied RGBA8 buffer. Each record holds path tags and points (move, line, quadratic, cubic, close), a premultiplied RGBA8 color, a nonzero or even-odd fill rule, and an affine matrix. The image is drawn with source-over compositing in a single call, Rasterize<TileDescriptor_8x16>(geometries, count, matrix, threads, image). It is a fill engine only: there are no strokes, gradients, images, clipping, blend modes or text layout, and the only input format is its own binary .vectorimage file ('Bvec' version 1, parsed by VectorImage). It is not a drop-in for Blend2D, Skia or CoreGraphics.
how_it_is_fast: Rendering runs in three parallel phases on a pthread worker pool sized to the online CPU count. (1) Paths are transformed, curves flattened in 24.8 fixed point, and the resulting lines binned per path into 16-pixel-tall tile rows, with start-of-row cover values, all in parallel across paths. (2) Per-row lists of contributing paths are built in parallel bands. (3) Each 16-row band is rasterized independently in paint order. Rasterization uses exact-area cover/area accumulation into a dense per-band int32 table, plus a bit vector of touched cells that is walked with popcount and count-trailing-zeros to emit spans. Fully covered runs are filled from the carried cover, and spans are composited with 64-bit SWAR source-over, with a store-only fast path for opaque spans and for zero destination pixels. Per-thread bump allocators avoid malloc during a frame.
when_to_use: Rendering very large, static, fill-only vector scenes (maps, CAD or GIS layers, pre-flattened text) at high resolution on a many-core Apple Silicon Mac, where one frame has tens of thousands of paths.
WebAssembly apps that can enable SharedArrayBuffer (cross-origin isolation headers) and want a multi-threaded software rasterizer; the repo ships an Emscripten build script and demo.
As a reference design for band-parallel scanline rasterization (sparse cell accumulation with bit vectors) when building your own renderer.
When geometry is already converted to fills with premultiplied solid colors, and you need throughput rather than a full 2D API.
when_not_to_use: You need a general 2D API (strokes, dashes, gradients, images, clipping, text, blend modes): use Blend2D, Skia or another full library.
Windows, which is unsupported per the README. Linux builds also need a patch, because Threads.cpp calls the Darwin-only pthread_set_qos_class_self_np on every non-Emscripten build.

Single-core or low-core targets, or small scenes: the design relies on parallelism, the README makes no single-thread claim, and a search snippet of a Hacker News comment says Blend2D beats Blaze in some tests on x86_64.

Production use that needs support: code is essentially unchanged since June 2023, and correctness reports go unanswered. Issue #8 (open) says the Paris-30k output differs from Inkscape's, issue #4 (open since 2023-10) reports a broken Tiger render with suspected threading problems, and issue #7 (radiation symbol defect) was closed with no fix commit.

integration.form: source-drop (Blaze/ directory: header templates plus 9 .cpp files; no CMake or library target)
integration.dependencies: none beyond POSIX threads and the C11 <stdatomic.h> header used from C++
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 with Clang: the Xcode demo uses gnu++20 with Release at -Ofast and SIMD_NEON=1, and the WebAssembly build uses em++ -O3 -std=c++20 -fno-rtti -fno-exceptions. GCC builds are not shown.
integration.platforms: macOS (arm64 NEON path or generic C++) and WebAssembly with pthreads; other POSIX systems after patching the QoS call; no Windows
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Rasterization is internally parallel. A Threads instance owns one shared task list, so do not run two Rasterize calls on the same Threads object concurrently. Its worker threads are never joined or stopped (~Threads is empty).

gotchas: Colors must be premultiplied RGBA8, and the destination must be cleared by the caller. Call Threads::ResetFrameMemory after each frame (the benchmark does), or per-frame bump memory keeps growing.
There is no SVG importer: issue #6 asks for the converter that produced the .vectorimage files, and it is not published, so you build Geometry arrays yourself.

Matrix::PreMultiply computed the wrong translation component until the 2024-09-30 fix (issue #5). The benchmark is unaffected because per-path transforms are identity and the frame matrix is scale plus translate, but older copies are wrong under rotation or skew.

Curve flattening uses fixed tolerances: quadratics are split until the control point lies within 0.125 px (L1) of the chord midpoint, and cubics until each second difference is at most 0.5 px. That bounds the deviation at roughly 0.18 px (derived from LinearizerUtils.h). Coordinates are quantized to 1/256 px.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Blaze over Blend2D only for fill-only scenes on many-core macOS or WebAssembly where you can feed pre-converted geometry, and only after benchmarking against a current Blend2D. Blend2D is maintained, full-featured, cross-platform and has its own multi-threaded context. Over Vello CPU, AGG or tiny-skia, Blaze's case is solely parallel fill throughput in C++. Those siblings offer strokes, paints and active maintenance.
verified_claims_summary: The claim exists only in search snippets of the author's blocked article. On an Apple M1 Max (10 cores), Paris-30k (50,681 paths, drawn at 2x scale to 4222x3474) takes 18 ms with Blaze, 47 ms with Blend2D (2023-era, multi-threaded with threadCount = hardware threads), 190 ms with Skia and 390 ms with CoreGraphics. The harness renders 500 times and averages the middle 490 whole-millisecond system_clock readings. The repo's adapters show that Skia (SkCanvas::MakeRasterDirect) and CoreGraphics (CGBitmapContext) run single-threaded, so the 10.6x and about 20x figures mostly reflect 10 cores against 1. Blend2D is the only like-for-like (multi-threaded) baseline, and its BLContext is created and ended inside every timed frame. Anti-aliasing is the same class for Blaze and Blend2D (analytic area coverage), but no image comparison is published. The harness also has three output-equivalence flaws. The Skia adapter passes Blaze's premultiplied colors to SkPaint::setColor, which expects unpremultiplied ARGB, so Skia draws Paris-30k's 33,171 translucent paths (of 50,681) with wrong colors. All three baseline adapters ignore each path's fill rule, so they draw Tiger's 235 even-odd paths as nonzero (Paris-30k is all nonzero). The CoreGraphics adapter leaves path and color pointers uninitialized for fully transparent paths (none in Paris-30k). None of these changes the work much, but the outputs are not identical. No compiler, flags, library versions or result files are published, and the Benchmarks/ files have no build file.
status_note: Stale (feature work ended June 2023; the last commits on 2024-09-30 are a matrix fix and cleanup; three open issues without replies). It is MIT and small enough to vendor, but treat it as a research codebase, not a maintained library.
